description: Plan step L5 (design step S4 first half; graph node schedules). Bind time-triggered entries to the main agent's session through the DSH schedule service, deliver messages with the wake table, the holder states, task removal with its records, and loops:schedule-tools (blocks from the day the row is enabled). Deletes DSH tasks, which is irreversible: deep review. Probe required. Depends on FEAT-011.
steps: Read loops design sec 6.2 (time: dsh-schedule, reconciliation items 0..n, fingerprint, 'prove it is ours and useless before deleting', removed-tasks.jsonl, entry-gone wait F41), 6.4 (holder states ok/none/archived/missing/elsewhere/unknown, writer-held 5-minute mark, held messages 24 h, deliver table, resolveAgent error codes, to: event-session), 2.4 row 16 (loops:schedule-tools: refuse changes of board tasks through DSH schedule tools and refuse schedule_create whose text starts with 'Loop board: '), 10.1/10.2 (host contract and unverified items V12-V17), 11.3 (irreversible places), 16 S4. Read impl-plan Interpretations 4 and 5. Read reference/dsh-desktop-0.2.1-rc.3 dsh-schedule (selector shapes, schedule:1052-1059 etc.), dsh-tool-schedule, dsh-api-session-controller (resolveAgent), dsh-workspace (list/archivedSessionIds, workspace/session-stop) in the MAIN checkout before coding.

Holder location (Interpretations 5): holder.ts reads the main agent through the existing mainAgentOf(userHome, dir) / readHolder(holderFileOf(...)) in src/graph/main-agent-holder.ts, behind ONE function holderRecordFor(projectRoot) so that M3's later move into the project's .llm/ changes only that function. Do not edit src/graph/main-agent-holder.ts.

Specs first (new tests/loops-bind.spec.ts and tests/loops-deliver.spec.ts; extend tests/fake-rc3.ts with a schedule service (create, list, catalog, delete, update shapes, whole-key decoding, schedule/changed, delivery of a message with source 'schedule' at the due time), sessionController.resolveAgent with session/not-found and session/writer-held, workspaceRegistry.archivedSessionIds (including a throw) and workspace/session-stop, live agent followup/steer/inject recording target and status): creating, moving to a new main agent session, changing back what someone edited on DSH's task page (and writing one explaining line), orphans, archive handling; reconciliation never deletes a task unless it is provably the board's own and no longer needed, and writes the full text to removed-tasks.jsonl first, and does not delete when that file cannot be written; removeTask has eight reasons each with one case, plus: holder state elsewhere/unknown -> tasks bound to the holder session are kept (return 'kept'), state none only deletes after two consecutive reconciliations, entry-gone waits as designed; messages with no main agent are held 24 h then discarded; archived or missing session -> treated as no main agent with the page/home-line text 'main agent session archived: type /wish here'; session open in another DSH process -> run lock handed to that process, retry every 5 minutes, 'cannot hand over' after 5 minutes; the agent/pre-step line and the two walk records last-step.json and main-step.json; deliver uses steer for running, inject when idle with active goal, followup otherwise, per the wake table; loops:schedule-tools denies the three call kinds (edit/delete/update of a board task by id or name pattern, schedule_create beginning with 'Loop board: ', and any bypass listed in sec 6.2), allows unrelated schedule_create; guard rule installed like graph-files-only, no shadow, violation record rule 'loops:schedule-tools'.

Implement src/loops/holder.ts, bind.ts, deliver.ts, remove.ts, reminder.ts and the schedule-tools rule in src/loops/guard.ts; wire in src/loops/index.ts; add the rule to GUARD_RULES with its contract test line; add typed minimal schedule / sessionController / workspaceRegistry members to src/shared/dsh-min.ts with the rc.3 evidence in comments. Every host call inside timers and listeners is wrapped; a throw degrades row health with the reason and never leaves a half-created or half-deleted task without a record.

Probe: extend scenario loops: bind a task to the main-agent session with the shifted clock, the due-time delivery reaches the session, schedule/changed is received, loops:schedule-tools blocks the three calls, a session archived by stopActivity makes the task removed with the record and the entry returns 'held'. Record the outcomes of V12-V17 in findings (or why they cannot be verified).

Docs: ORCHESTRATION.md loop board section (binding, delivery, removal), DESIGN.md. Commit at most three times (holder+deliver; bind+remove; guard+probe+docs). Messages carry gate results including the probe exit code.
acceptance_criteria: No DSH task is deleted unless it is provably the board's own and useless; its full text is in removed-tasks.jsonl before the delete; an unreadable holder or an 'elsewhere' session keeps tasks.
loops:schedule-tools blocks from the day the row is enabled (L2 and probe).
The holder location is behind one function; src/graph/main-agent-holder.ts is unchanged.
build, preflight, npm test and npm run probe exit 0 (or only the recorded baseline failures); row still disabled in the patch.
verification: npm test (TEMP = system temp directory) exits 0
npm run probe exits 0 (scenario loops included)
findings:
Commit c6fbf24 on rules-loops-impl (pushed to origin, one commit rather than the three the step allowed: the pieces do not stand without each other and nothing in between would have been green). Gates on the committed tree, one at a time: npm run build 0, npm run preflight 0, npm test 0 (tests/rules-tickets.spec.ts did not show its intermittent timing failure this run, so it was not re-run), npm run probe 0 at 195/195 (194/194 before this step; one new check in scenario loops). Lint: eslint 249 suppressed (was 250: `npm run lint:update` pruned one stale suppression in tests/fake-rc3.ts that an eslint --fix of this step's files made unused; baselines only shrink), knip 21, jscpd 2 clones. Both the rules and the loops rows stay disabled: true in packages/hourness/cordis.patch.yml. docs/graph was deliberately not written (the step instruction forbade it), so the graph entry for this FEAT still has to be made by the caller.

DSH contract facts verified by reading reference/dsh-desktop-0.2.1-rc.3 (cited in src/shared/dsh-min.ts beside each new type): schedule service name and members (schedule:1992 `super(ctx, "schedule")`; create 2083-2112 with its title rules 93-97, exactly-one-selector check and the snake_case selector keys at/after_seconds/every_seconds/daily/weekly/cron, every_seconds >= 60 at schedule:21; list 2120-2122 returns only the active records of one session; catalog 2129-2136 adds sessionId/status/lastDelivery and sorts by scheduledAt then id; delete 2164-2182 hard-removes the row and its deliveries; update 2197-2224 over resolveScheduleUpdate 1806-1837, whose `expected` is decoded by whole key set (74-77, decoders 256-312/356-365/411-421/463-472) so a catalog row is invalid_rule, a mismatch is schedule_conflict, and a normalized-equal change answers updated:false without a code; change carries exactly kind plus its selector, 1710-1716; reminderTargetRefusal 2254-2261 refuses only a delegated child's session, so an archived session is accepted; emitChanged 2231-2237 after every write; the host's own delivery 1576-1625 with createUserMessage source {kind:'schedule'}, followup, sessions.flush and lastDelivery {scheduledAt, deliveredAt, messageId}; the reminder framing and its schedule_id_json / reminders_json at 1386-1418; no automatic retry 1627-1640). workspaceRegistry (dsh-workspace:376 service name, archivedSessionIds getter 506-508, list 454-460, requireState throws 934-937, archiveSession with stopActivity writes the set then sends workspace/session-stop 526-541 and 621-629). sessionController.resolveAgent (api-session-controller:3037-3039 delegating to 210-246, error codes session/not-found 237, session/writer-held 243, gateway/internal 244). The model-facing tool names and arguments (dsh-tool-schedule: schedule_create 508 with prompt/title/selectors, schedule_list 548, schedule_delete 570 with id, schedule_update 600 with id/title/prompt/selectors, and the update path reading `expected` from list). tests/fake-rc3.ts's fakeSchedule reproduces those refusals and normalizations, so a reconciliation that broke review F7 would fail at L2 as it would on the real host.

What a reviewer must check:
1. remove.ts is the only caller of schedule.delete (grep); its two conditions and the write-before-delete order; that a failure to append removed-tasks.jsonl returns kept and degrades the row (covered, but it is the irreversible path).
2. bind.ts item order: orphans are taken back BEFORE anything is made. The design lists item 4 last; taken literally, a lost state.json makes a second reminder and then deletes the first with its delivery history, which is what review F13 forbids. The order here is adopt, then make/move/repair, then remove what is left, with a `gone` set so the pass does not judge a task it just deleted.
3. holder.ts crosses the record with the session's main-agent projection only when the session is open in this process; when it is not, the record stands. A reviewer should decide whether that asymmetry is right (it never deletes on a reading it could not take, which is the safe direction).
4. The holder location really is one function (holderRecordFor) and src/graph/main-agent-holder.ts is unchanged (git diff).
5. deliver.ts now imports the rules board's wake table (src/rules/wake.ts `wayTo`, newly exported) so the two boards cannot drift apart; that is a cross-row import of a pure function, like src/loops/* already importing src/rules/store.ts.
6. The three calls loops:schedule-tools judges are covered at L2 only (see the gap list below).

Design gaps and deliberate narrowings:
1. entry-gone: design 6.2 names two certainties (the person deleted it, or the source that owns it handed over a replacement without it). Only the first is implemented, plus the 5-minute warm-up and two reconciliations 60 s apart. The registry (FEAT-009) does not expose each source's hand-over history, so the second cannot be read; wiring it needs a registry change and is left out of this step.
2. The step line of design 6.4 is `Loop run <run> for <entry>.`, which assumes the run id exists at the step. It only does after the reconciliation has seen lastDelivery, so the step notice runs one reconciliation first and falls back to `Loop board reminder for <entry>.` when the run is still unknown (for instance when the catalog cannot be read). The design should say which.
3. The 1/5/15-minute retries of a delivery live in memory, not in state.json: a host restart between them loses the retry, and the run stays as loop-fired without loop-done, which design 6.4 already reads as 'may repeat run'. Persisting them was not worth a second write path here.
4. `elsewhere` degrades the row after five unbroken minutes; the runtime measures that with an in-memory stamp (elsewhereSince), so a restart restarts the five minutes.
5. A project runtime built without a host context (the specs' worldOf) reports 'cannot read the main agent's record' as a degraded line. That is the design's text for a record that cannot be read, and it is honest, but it means the no-host test world always carries one degraded line; tests/loops-run.spec.ts was changed to expect it rather than hiding it.
6. Design 6.1's hand-over now really fires: holderHere reads the record and asks the live-agent registry. `handedElsewhere`, which makes holderState `elsewhere` with reason `handover`, is taken from the lock's own release record rather than from a second read of handover.json, so between a release and the other process taking the lock this process says `elsewhere` for that session. It never deletes in that state, which is the safe direction.
7. Not verifiable at L3 in this harness: V1 (ctx.get('schedule') from this row), V2 (schedule/changed reaching this row), V3 and V16 (resolveAgent from this row, and its two error codes), V14 and V15 (workspaceRegistry.archivedSessionIds and workspace/session-stop from this row), V17 (workspaceRegistry.list at activation), and the three calls loops:schedule-tools judges. The headless template (dsh-base + dsh-headless) mounts neither dsh-schedule nor the session controller, so DSH's four reminder tools are not registered and no reminder of the board can exist; the existing `loops` scenario pins 'no session controller', so those rows cannot be added to it. Verifying them needs either a new L3 scenario that mounts the Web composition's schedule and session-controller rows (one more host boot, unknown composition risk) or desktop L4. V12 (ctx.inject over this package's own service) stays as FEAT-009 left it. The probe check added here pins that both gates are installed on the real runtime and that the row says so.
8. Design 6.4's account-level part (scope 'machine', told.json) and 6.9's peak table are FEAT-013 and M6 work; last-step.json is written here, nothing reads it yet.
